meta.title: Reviewed banking-access disruptions
meta.about: Each event is entered by hand from its sources and reviewed. country_code is ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 (SSD, PSE, XKX and ESH are mapped to Natural Earth's SDS, PSX, KOS and SAH). event_type: technical_outage, withdrawal_limits, capital_controls, deposit_freeze or bank_failure. severity 1-5 (see docs/banking-access.md). confidence: social, multiple_reports or official. affected_people_est or affected_population_pct may be null when no source gives the reach: the map then shows the extent as unknown. Times are ISO 8601; resolved_time null means ongoing. Use 'official' only when a regulator, central bank or the bank itself is among the sources. last_verified_time is when a reviewer last confirmed the status (still ongoing, or resolved); an ongoing event not re-verified for 30 days counts half and says so on its card.

events.affected_basis: No source counts the people under the withdrawal limits. For scale only: a February 2026 Ankura study estimated that about 550,000 depositors may not recover their savings even within the proposed USD 100,000 ceiling.
events.summary: Informal capital controls since the 2019 crisis: deposits held in banks, cash withdrawals capped by central bank circulars 158 and 166 (reported raised to USD 800 and USD 400 a month in June 2025). A deposit recovery law was still under debate in spring 2026.

sources.title: Debate grows: Lebanon banking plan may leave 550,000 depositors without full repayment
Lebanon's central bank open to raising withdrawal limits under conditions, sources say
Lebanon conflict likely to block deposit refund plan

events.affected_basis: No source counts the people cut off. For scale only: press reports of almost 3 million clients (Perfil; El Cronista says 3 million); clients are not verified as unique people. Insured deposits (up to 75 minimum wages) are being paid from the Deposit Guarantee Fund; one report says about 1.2 million clients were refunded within two days.
events.summary: The Central Bank of Paraguay opened a resolution procedure for ueno bank on 2 November 2026 after its solvency ratio fell below half the required minimum, and suspended its services. The central bank says the case is specific to this bank.

events.affected_basis: No source gives the number of clients. The bank held just under 3% of Serbian banking assets. The National Bank of Serbia's own notice was not found; the decision is reported as quoted from it.
events.summary: The National Bank of Serbia's executive board revoked ALTA banka's licence on 30 October 2026 and found the conditions for bankruptcy met; accounts, cards and branches were suspended. The Deposit Insurance Agency is to pay insured deposits (up to EUR 50,000) within seven working days.
